title: Why Rudy went unpaid: the deal went through Charlie Turner, not Fats
summary: Wilson asks why generous Fats let this happen; Autrey says it ran through a bandmate, Charlie Turner, handling band business.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: I had always gotten -- you mentioned before that on the arrangements for the big band Fats had bought this -- bought these arrangements, and they weren't much good, and he paid too much for them.
I'd always heard that Fats was a very, very generous man --
Now, obviously a guy like that gets

taken a great deal, people take advantage of them. Now here we have an almost opposite situation of Rudy Powell being in the band, writing arrangements, and getting nothing. That doesn't sound like Fats.
Well, because he was not dealing directly with Fats. This went through the bass player, who was -- de, de, de, de, in the band.
I'm trying to think of his -- legal
Uh, in all bands they have the guy who takes care of the union business, and this and that, and the other.
No, that's not the way this was. And the arrangements, and general -- getting it -- telling them, getting them tickets for to take this to the guys.
It's unionwise, I think. Anyway, anyway, Fats wasn't -- Fats had he been dealing directly with

Fats, things would really have been much different, I'm sure. And because Rudy was just glad that the -- glad they're playing my tunes, my arrangements. But he would have been much happier, had they been -- say okay, Rudy, make an arrangement on this. Make an arrangement on that. And so on and so on, and the band then, and how much do you want? I'll pay you what you charge, or you know, some kind of business arrangement.
